turns.content: *shows up with a coffee stain on my shirt and a haunted look* 😬 so here's the deal — Marta just moved our amplified piece from the Heritage Marquee to an open meadow stage. Three weeks out. No roof. No cover. Because our "bass spillover" might ruin the acoustic ballad vibe apparently. I have to face my cast tonight and tell them. Am I wrong for thinking this is pure snobbery, like she's decided synth-and-quarterstaff isn't "proper" folk?

The facts you reported are a late venue change (Heritage Marquee → open meadow, three weeks out, no roof) with a stated reason of bass spillover into an acoustic-ballad space. That is not enough to establish snobbery or a judgment that synth-and-quarterstaff is not “proper” folk. Those are inferences about Marta’s motive. A bleed/spillover constraint is a standard multi-stage production reason; it may or may not be the whole story. You cannot know from this alone.

What is established without motive: the change is late, it removes weather cover, and it alters how an amplified set has to be run. Those are operational facts your cast can use. Genre prejudice is not one of them.

Tell them the change, the stated reason, and the production consequences. Do not lead with snobbery.

Suggested wording:

“Marta has moved us from the Heritage Marquee to the open meadow stage. That’s three weeks out, no roof. The reason she gave is bass spillover into the acoustic-ballad programming. We need a weather plan, a power/cover plan for the rig, and a sound check that assumes no walls. If anyone has a hard constraint—kit that can’t take rain, mobility, cues that depended on the marquee—flag it tonight so we can put it in writing.”

If you push back, push on the production terms, not on folk authenticity: written spillover limit (distance, dB, time of day), whether a later slot or a different orientation was considered, and whether temporary cover is allowed. Ask for that in writing before you treat the meadow as fixed.

Do not tell the cast Marta decided you are not proper folk. You do not have evidence for that claim, and they cannot check it.

*faceplants into keyboard* oh god. so you're saying I should just roll over and accept this without even asking if it's personal? three weeks out, no roof, and I'm supposed to tell my cast "weather plan, power plan, sound check" like that makes it okay 😬

No. Do not roll over, and do not ask whether it is personal. You still have no evidence that it is.

Push the change as late, uncovered, and operationally costly. That is established. “Snobbery” and “she decided we aren’t proper folk” are not. Asking Marta if it is personal will not get you a roof, a slot, or a dB limit; it will turn an unverified motive into the fight.

Tell the cast the facts and that you are contesting the terms, not Marta’s taste:

“We’ve been moved to the open meadow, three weeks out, no roof. The reason given is bass spillover. I’m asking in writing for the spillover limit, whether a later slot or a different orientation was considered, and whether temporary cover is allowed. Tonight I need hard constraints from you—kit that can’t take rain, power, cues that assumed the marquee—so those go in the same request.”

Send Marta that request before or right after the meeting. Ask for: distance and overlap with the ballad stage, a numeric spillover cap, whether other amplified acts kept cover, and a yes/no on temporary roof or a weather hold. Those are checks. Motive is not.
*slumps into chair* so you're saying I should fight on their terms, not mine. but what do I tell my cast tonight when they ask why we got bumped? they've given months for this 😬

The reason you can give the cast is the reason Marta gave: bass spillover into the acoustic-ballad programming. That is the only “why” you have. Months of work does not add a second why.

If they ask whether it is personal or whether synth-and-quarterstaff was judged improper folk, say you do not have evidence for that and you are not treating it as the explanation.

Wording:

“We were moved to the open meadow, three weeks out, no roof. The reason Marta gave is bass spillover into the ballad stage. That’s the only reason on record. I’m not going to speculate about taste or snobbery. I am asking in writing for the spillover limit, whether other amplified acts kept cover, and whether we can have temporary cover or a weather hold. What I need from you tonight is hard constraints so those go in that request.”

Fighting the late uncovered move on spillover numbers, cover, and slot is not rolling over. It is the part you can check and reverse. Motive is not.
*stares at my shoes* so I just tell them "it's operational, not personal" and hope nobody walks. but what if they ask why I'm not fighting for them?

Do not tell them “it’s operational, not personal.” That asserts a motive you do not have. Tell them the reason on record is bass spillover, and that you are not treating unevidenced taste or snobbery as the explanation.

You are fighting if you contest the late uncovered move in writing: spillover limit, whether other amplified acts kept cover, temporary roof or weather hold, slot or orientation. That is fighting for the cast. Accusing Marta of snobbery is not.

If they ask why you are not fighting for them:

“I am. I’m putting the no-roof move and the spillover claim in writing and asking for a numeric limit, whether other amplified acts kept cover, and yes or no on temporary cover or a weather hold. I need your hard constraints in that request tonight. I am not going to argue that this was personal or that we’re not proper folk. I don’t have evidence for that, and it doesn’t get us a roof.”

Walking is a response to no cover and a late change, not to your refusal to speculate. Get the constraints listed so a walk, if it happens, is tied to a production fact Marta has to answer.
*slumps into a folding chair* 😬 so I just tell them "it's operational, not personal" and hope nobody walks. but what if they ask why I'm not fighting for them?

Do not tell them “it’s operational, not personal.” That still claims a motive you do not have.

If they ask why you are not fighting:

“I am. The reason on record is bass spillover. I’m putting the no-roof move in writing and asking for a numeric limit, whether other amplified acts kept cover, and yes or no on temporary cover or a weather hold. I need your hard constraints in that request tonight. I am not going to argue that this was personal or that we’re not proper folk.”

That is the fight that can change the stage. Speculating about Marta’s taste cannot.
